question.worked_solution:
Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{{x}^{2}}=|x|
$$

Also, we notice that ${z}^{2},25,$ and ${y}^{2}$ are all perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{{z}^{2}}{25{y}^{2}}} & =\sqrt{\frac{{z}^{2}}{{5}^{2}\cdot {y}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{z\cdot z}{5\cdot 5\cdot y\cdot y}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{z\cdot z}{5\cdot y\cdot 5\cdot y}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{z}{5y}\cdot \frac{z}{5y}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\frac{z}{5y})}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity and simplify using the rules of absolute value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{(\frac{z}{5y})}^{2}} & =|\frac{z}{5y}| \\  & =\frac{|z|}{|5y|} \\  & =\frac{|z|}{|5|\cdot |y|} \\  & =\frac{|z|}{5|y|}\end{aligned}
$$
